components.note: 冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'
日 depicts the sun as a circle with a dot or short stroke inside — a simplified picture of the sun's disc, later squared off in the standard script.

example.hanzi: 他周日要去医院复查。
example.pinyin: tā zhōurì yào qù yīyuàn fùchá.
example.english: He needs to go back to the hospital for a checkup on Sunday.
example.fact: The Gregorian calendar's seven-day week has no astronomical basis — it traces back to ancient Babylon's fascination with seven visible celestial bodies (the sun, moon, and five planets). The Romans later spread the practice empire-wide, and it survived the fall of Rome to become the near-universal standard in use today.

meanings: (slang) to fail to catch anything (on a fishing trip)

components.note: 穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.
冖 here is a distorted form of 力 (strength) — a simplified way of showing soldiers grouped together.
车 (cart/vehicle) — 军 originally pictured soldiers riding out to battle in war chariots.

example.hanzi: 他的梦想是加入空军,成为一名飞行员。
example.pinyin: tā de mèngxiǎng shì jiārù kōngjūn, chéngwéi yī míng fēixíngyuán.
example.english: His dream is to join the air force and become a pilot.
example.fact: The Royal Air Force, founded in 1918, was the world's first air force established as a fully independent military branch, separate from the army and navy. Most other nations' air forces grew directly out of army aviation corps and only became independent services decades later.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 使 involves a person carrying out a task.
吏 (a government official) — 使 originally referred to an official sent to carry out orders, giving rise to the meaning 'to make someone do something' or 'to use.'
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'

example.hanzi: 长期缺水使得这片土地变成了沙漠。
example.pinyin: chángqī quēshuǐ shǐde zhè piàn tǔdì biànchéngle shāmò.
example.english: Long-term water scarcity caused this land to turn into a desert.
example.fact: The Aral Sea, once the world's fourth-largest lake, has shrunk by over 90% since the 1960s after Soviet irrigation projects diverted the rivers feeding it. Vast stretches of the former lakebed are now a new desert called the Aralkum, visible from space.

components.note: 上 (top) — the upper edge pressing down
卜 — the lower edge, with a card squeezed between the two
A pictograph of half of a split tree trunk, shown in cross-section (compare 爿, the other half) — the source of 片's meaning 'a thin slice, piece.'

example.hanzi: 她在生日卡片上写了一句祝福的话。
example.pinyin: tā zài shēngrì kǎpiàn shàng xiěle yī jù zhùfú de huà.
example.english: She wrote a blessing on the birthday card.
example.fact: The world's oldest surviving printed book, the Diamond Sutra from Dunhuang, China, was produced in AD 868 using woodblock printing — over five centuries before Gutenberg's press appeared in Europe.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, body) — 脱 relates to taking something off the body.
兑 (duì) gives a sound close to tuō, sharing a related initial.
A drawing of a robe's collar and folded sides, seen from the front.
無-shaped top pictures a dancer holding decorated sleeves or fans.
舛 below pictures a pair of feet, together giving 舞 its meaning 'to dance.'

example.hanzi: 那家夜店表演脱衣舞,吸引了不少游客。
example.pinyin: nà jiā yèdiàn biǎoyǎn tuōyīwǔ, xīyǐnle bùshǎo yóukè.
example.english: That nightclub performs striptease shows, attracting many tourists.
example.fact: Burlesque striptease as an American stage art traces back to the 1860s, when touring British troupes blended satire, comedy, and daring costume into a new form of variety theater — decades before it became associated with Las Vegas showmanship in the 20th century.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 健 describes a person's physical condition.
建 depicts building or constructing — a person strong enough to build things gave 健 its meaning 'strong, healthy.'
身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.

example.hanzi: 我每天下班后都会去健身房健身。
example.pinyin: wǒ měitiān xiàbān hòu dōu huì qù jiànshēnfáng jiànshēn.
example.english: I go to the gym to work out every day after work.
example.fact: Skeletal muscle is one of the few tissues that can meaningfully regenerate throughout adult life: resistance exercise triggers satellite cells at the edges of muscle fibers to fuse in and repair micro-tears. That repair process is part of why hypertrophy training requires rest days as much as effort.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'
亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'

example.hanzi: 水和油放在一起,过一会儿就会自然分离。
example.pinyin: shuǐ hé yóu fàng zài yīqǐ, guò yīhuǐr jiù huì zìrán fēnlí.
example.english: When water and oil are put together, they naturally separate after a while.
example.fact: Water and oil separate because water molecules are polar and strongly attract each other through hydrogen bonds, squeezing out nonpolar oil molecules that can't compete for the bonding. Industrial oil-spill skimmers exploit this same principle to draw crude oil off the surface of seawater.

components.note: The oracle-bone form pictured a person facing backward with an open mouth below, representing a ruler issuing commands aloud — the source of 后's early meaning 'queen, empress.' It was later borrowed as the simplified form of 後, meaning 'behind, after.'
门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.

example.hanzi: 小偷是从后门溜进屋子的。
example.pinyin: xiǎotōu shì cóng hòumén liū jìn wūzi de.
example.english: The thief slipped into the house through the back door.
example.fact: In 2010, security researchers discovered that the Stuxnet worm exploited a legitimate but undocumented backdoor in Siemens industrial control software to sabotage centrifuges at Iran's Natanz nuclear facility — one of the first cyberweapons known to cause physical damage to critical infrastructure.

components.note: 戈 (a dagger-axe, a weapon) — 战 relates to fighting and war.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 战 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match.
⺼ (flesh/body) — historically linked to physical strength and overcoming an opponent
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 胜's reading shèng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 中国女排在决赛中战胜了强劲的对手。
example.pinyin: zhōngguó nǚpái zài juésài zhōng zhànshèngle qiángjìng de duìshǒu.
example.english: The Chinese women's volleyball team defeated a strong opponent in the final.
example.fact: In the 1980 Winter Olympics 'Miracle on Ice,' a team of American college and amateur players defeated the heavily favored Soviet squad, which had won gold in five of the previous six Olympics — one of the most celebrated upsets in sports history.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 佛 refers to an enlightened being, the Buddha
弗 (fú) gives the sound — an exact match with 佛's reading fú
罒 (net) — relates to 罗's original meaning 'net for catching birds,' extended to 'to gather, collect' and used today as a common Chinese surname.
田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 达's meaning 'to reach, arrive, achieve.'
大 (dà) gives the sound — 达 is pronounced dá, a close match sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 他们计划下个月去佛罗里达度假。
example.pinyin: tāmen jìhuà xià gè yuè qù Fóluólǐdá dùjià.
example.english: They plan to vacation in Florida next month.
example.fact: NASA deliberately built the Kennedy Space Center on Florida's Atlantic coast in the 1960s partly because launching rockets eastward near the equator lets them borrow extra speed from Earth's own rotation, saving fuel that a launch from a site farther north would have to burn instead.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 倒 relates to a person falling over
到 (dào) gives the sound — 倒 is also pronounced dào, an exact match
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: 那棵老树在暴风雨中轰然倒下。
example.pinyin: nà kē lǎoshù zài bàofēngyǔ zhōng hōngrán dǎoxià.
example.english: The old tree collapsed with a crash in the storm.
example.fact: Redwood trees can weigh over 1,000 tons and grow past 100 meters tall, yet their root systems rarely extend more than 3-4 meters deep. They survive storms largely by spreading their roots wide and intertwining them with neighboring redwoods, effectively holding each other up underground.

components.note: 田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'
氵 (water) — 汁 names a liquid.
十 (shí) gives a sound distantly related to zhī, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 妈妈每天早上都会榨新鲜的果汁给我喝。
example.pinyin: māma měitiān zǎoshang dōu huì zhà xīnxiān de guǒzhī gěi wǒ hē.
example.english: Mom squeezes fresh fruit juice for me to drink every morning.
example.fact: In 1747, Scottish naval surgeon James Lind ran one of the first controlled clinical trials, discovering that citrus fruit cured scurvy among sailors — decades before vitamin C was even identified, in 1932, as the compound actually responsible.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 被 originally meant a quilt or covering, like a blanket.
皮 (pí) gives a hint of the sound — 被 is pronounced bèi, a connection that has shifted over time.
辶 (to walk) — pressing close on someone's heels ties to 迫's meaning 'to press, to force.'
白 (bái) gives a sound distantly related to pò, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 由于资金短缺,公司被迫裁员。
example.pinyin: yóuyú zījīn duǎnquē, gōngsī bèipò cáiyuán.
example.english: Due to a funding shortage, the company was forced to lay off staff.
example.fact: When Krakatoa erupted in 1883, the blast was heard over 3,000 miles away in Mauritius, and life on the devastated island was forced to restart from almost nothing. The very first colonizers to reach the sterilized island were spiders, arriving on wind-blown silk within months of the eruption.

components.note: A simple picture of a tuft of animal fur or a feather, its curving strokes suggesting soft, wispy strands — the source of 毛's meaning 'hair, fur, wool.'
巾 depicts a piece of cloth draped over a rod — its simple vertical lines mirror a hanging towel or curtain.

example.hanzi: 他用毛巾擦干了头发。
example.pinyin: tā yòng máojīn cāgānle tóufǎ.
example.english: He dried his hair with a towel.
example.fact: Terry cloth towels get their absorbency from thousands of small uncut loops of cotton yarn woven into the base fabric, which dramatically increases surface area — a single terry towel can expose several times more fiber surface than a flat cotton sheet of the same size.

meanings: the great bulk of the population

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
人 (person), tripled — three people together depict a crowd, giving 众 its meaning 'many, multitude.'

example.hanzi: 这部电影深受大众喜爱。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng shēn shòu dàzhòng xǐ'ài.
example.english: This movie is deeply loved by the general public.
example.fact: Henry Ford's moving assembly line, introduced in 1913, cut the time to build a Model T chassis from about 12 hours to roughly 90 minutes. That efficiency let Ford slash prices repeatedly, turning the automobile from a luxury item into something the general public could actually afford.

components.note: 犭 (dog) — 狂 originally described a mad, rabid dog, extending to 'wild, crazy.'
王 (wáng) gives a sound distantly related to kuáng, having drifted apart over time.
又 is a simplified stand-in for the original phonetic component 雚 (guān), whose pronunciation echoes 欢's reading huān.
欠 depicts a person with mouth open, exhaling — an image tied to sighs, shouts, and exclamations of delight, giving 欢 its meaning 'happy, joyous.'

example.hanzi: 巴西的狂欢节吸引了来自世界各地的游客。
example.pinyin: bāxī de kuánghuānjié xīyǐnle láizì shìjiè gèdì de yóukè.
example.english: Brazil's carnival attracts tourists from all over the world.
example.fact: Rio de Janeiro's Carnival parade features samba schools competing inside a purpose-built stadium called the Sambadrome, completed in 1984. Each school gets roughly an hour to march about 700 meters while judges score costumes, choreography, and drumming in real time.

components.note: 木 (tree) — traditionally read as a tree that has borne fruit.
立 (standing) — standing close by to watch it grow, evoking closeness and nurture, extended to 亲's meaning 'close, dear; parent, relative.'
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 这件毛衣是奶奶亲手织的。
example.pinyin: zhè jiàn máoyī shì nǎinai qīnshǒu zhī de.
example.english: This sweater was knitted by grandma with her own hands.
example.fact: A traditional hand-tied Persian carpet can contain over one million individual knots per square meter, each tied by hand. A skilled weaver working steadily might still take a full year to complete a single large rug.

components.note: Roof — a house shut in quiet stillness.
Gives the sound shū, related to jì but drifted apart over time.
宀 (roof) — an older semantic link to being shut away alone indoors.
莫 (mò) gives the sound — an exact match with 寞.

example.hanzi: 退休以后,他常常感到寂寞。
example.pinyin: tuìxiū yǐhòu, tā chángcháng gǎndào jìmò.
example.english: After retiring, he often feels lonely.
example.fact: Psychologist John Cacioppo's longitudinal research found that chronic loneliness raises cortisol levels and disrupts sleep in ways comparable to physical stressors. Several large follow-up studies have since linked sustained social isolation to mortality risk on par with smoking roughly 15 cigarettes a day.

components.note: Depicts a young wheat or tree branch that has not yet borne fruit — the image of something still incomplete, the source of 未's meaning 'not yet.'
女 (woman) — 婚 relates to marriage, historically centered on the wife.
昏 (hūn) gives the sound — an exact match with 婚.
大 (a grown man) — the figure being depicted.
一 (a hairpin) — worn across the top of the head to mark a coming-of-age ceremony, giving 夫 its meaning 'man, husband.'

example.hanzi: 她带着未婚夫回家见父母。
example.pinyin: tā dàizhe wèihūnfū huí jiā jiàn fùmǔ.
example.english: She brought her fiancé home to meet her parents.
example.fact: The tradition of a diamond engagement ring is largely a 20th-century marketing invention: De Beers' 1947 ad campaign coined the slogan 'A Diamond Is Forever,' turning what had been a relatively uncommon gift into an expected part of Western marriage proposals within a couple of decades.

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates to 清's meaning 'clear (water), pure.'
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 清 is also pronounced qīng, an exact match.
阝 (a mound/settlement) — represents a city or town.
余 (surplus, remainder) — the leftover waste a city produces, which must be cleared away, giving 除 its meaning 'to remove, eliminate.'

example.hanzi: 工人们正在清除路上的积雪。
example.pinyin: gōngrénmen zhèngzài qīngchú lù shàng de jīxuě.
example.english: Workers are clearing away the snow on the road.
example.fact: Japan's Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route cuts through the 'Yuki-no-Otani' snow corridor, where plows carve a road between walls of snow that can tower over 20 meters — among the tallest man-made snow canyons on Earth, cleared fresh each spring.

components.note: 酋 pictures a jar of wine.
寸 (hand) below offers it up respectfully, giving 尊 its meaning 'to respect, to honor.'

The traditional form 嚴 pictured a person shouting orders (吅, two mouths) from a cliff or gorge (厂) — the image of a stern command echoing off rock walls, giving 严 its meaning 'strict, severe.' The simplified form keeps only a stylized trace of that scene.

example.hanzi: 每个人都应该有尊严地生活。
example.pinyin: měi gè rén dōu yīnggāi yǒu zūnyán de shēnghuó.
example.english: Everyone should live with dignity.
example.fact: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1948, opens its very first article by asserting that all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights — a direct response to the atrocities of World War II.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 演 originally described water flowing and spreading out, later extended to 'developing, unfolding'
寅 (yín) gives a sound distantly related to 演's reading yǎn, having drifted apart over time
又 (hand) shows a hand performing an action.
戈 (spear) — mock combat and stage tricks with weapons gave 戏 its meaning 'play, drama.'

example.hanzi: 他从小就喜欢在学校演戏。
example.pinyin: tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuān zài xuéxiào yǎnxì.
example.english: He has loved performing plays at school since childhood.
example.fact: The Theatre of Dionysus in Athens, carved into the slope of the Acropolis around the 6th century BC, could seat roughly 17,000 spectators. It's considered the birthplace of Western drama, hosting the original performances of plays by Sophocles and Euripides.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'
亻 (person) — 位 relates to a person's location.
立 (to stand) — the spot where a person stands gave 位 its meaning 'position' or 'place,' and later, a polite measure word for people.

example.hanzi: 手机的定位功能帮我们找到了最近的餐厅。
example.pinyin: shǒujī de dìngwèi gōngnéng bāng wǒmen zhǎodàole zuìjìn de cāntīng.
example.english: The phone's positioning function helped us find the nearest restaurant.
example.fact: GPS satellites carry atomic clocks accurate to within a few billionths of a second, but under Einstein's relativity, their onboard clocks actually run faster than clocks on Earth's surface. Engineers deliberately slow them down before launch by about 38 microseconds a day to keep positioning accurate.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 没 originally meant to sink or drown in water, later extended to the negative 'not have.'
殳 (shū) is the historical sound component; it no longer rhymes with méi in modern Mandarin, another case of sound drift over time.
冫 (water) — 准 originally referred to a carpenter's level using water to check flatness, extended to 'standard, accurate, level.'
隹 (zhuī) gives a sound hint — 准 is pronounced zhǔn, sharing the base sound though the vowel and tone differ somewhat.

example.hanzi: 他没准明天就回来了。
example.pinyin: tā méizhǔn míngtiān jiù huílái le.
example.english: He might come back tomorrow, who knows.
example.fact: Even with supercomputers, weather forecasts lose most of their reliability beyond about two weeks — a consequence of chaos theory's 'butterfly effect,' first modeled by meteorologist Edward Lorenz in 1961 when rounding a variable to three decimal places instead of six produced a wildly different simulated forecast.

components.note: 艹 (plant) sits on top.
心, literally 'heart,' here represents the central core inside a plant stem — together giving 芯 its meaning 'pith, wick, core' (as in a lamp wick or battery core).
A pictograph of half of a split tree trunk, shown in cross-section (compare 爿, the other half) — the source of 片's meaning 'a thin slice, piece.'

example.hanzi: 这款手机使用了最新的芯片。
example.pinyin: zhè kuǎn shǒujī shǐyòngle zuìxīn de xīnpiàn.
example.english: This phone uses the latest chip.
example.fact: In 1965, Intel co-founder Gordon Moore observed that the number of transistors on an integrated circuit was doubling roughly every two years — a prediction now known as Moore's Law that held remarkably well for over five decades before physical limits began to slow it in the 2020s.

components.note: 木 (tree/wood) — 核 originally named the hard pit inside a fruit.
亥 (hài) gives an approximate sound, close to hé though the vowel has since shifted.
弓 (bow) — 弹 relates to a projectile shot from a bow, like a pellet
单 (dān) gives a loose sound connection to 弹's reading dàn

example.hanzi: 这部纪录片讲述了核弹研发的历史。
example.pinyin: zhè bù jìlùpiàn jiǎngshùle hédàn yánfā de lìshǐ.
example.english: This documentary tells the history of nuclear bomb development.
example.fact: The largest nuclear weapon ever detonated, the Soviet 'Tsar Bomba' tested in 1961 over Novaya Zemlya, released roughly 3,300 times the energy of the Hiroshima bomb. Its shockwave reportedly broke windows in Norway and Finland, over 500 miles away.

meanings: unit (group of people as a whole)

components.note: The traditional form 單 pictured a forked hunting tool resembling a slingshot or bola, used to bring down a single target — the source of 单's meaning 'single, only one.'
亻 (person) — 位 relates to a person's location.
立 (to stand) — the spot where a person stands gave 位 its meaning 'position' or 'place,' and later, a polite measure word for people.

example.hanzi: 他所在的单位负责这个项目的管理。
example.pinyin: tā suǒzài de dānwèi fùzé zhège xiàngmù de guǎnlǐ.
example.english: The organization he works for is responsible for managing this project.
example.fact: In 2019, the kilogram — the last SI base unit still defined by a physical object, a platinum-iridium cylinder locked in a Paris vault since 1889 — was redefined in terms of the Planck constant, finally freeing the entire metric system from dependence on a single physical artifact.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
立 here depicts a tongue positioned to speak.
日 here depicts an open mouth — a tongue forming sound in the mouth gave 音 its meaning 'sound, tone.'
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.

example.hanzi: 爷爷喜欢每天早上听收音机里的新闻。
example.pinyin: yéye xǐhuān měitiān zǎoshang tīng shōuyīnjī lǐ de xīnwén.
example.english: Grandpa likes listening to the news on the radio every morning.
example.fact: In 1920, Pittsburgh station KDKA broadcast the results of the Harding-Cox presidential election, one of the first scheduled commercial radio broadcasts in the U.S. Within just a few years, radio ownership exploded from a hobbyist niche into a fixture of millions of American homes.

components.note: 手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.
钅 (metal) — 铐 names metal shackles or handcuffs.
考 (kǎo) gives a sound close to 铐's reading kào, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 警察给逃跑的嫌疑人戴上了手铐。
example.pinyin: jǐngchá gěi táopǎo de xiányírén dàishàngle shǒukào.
example.english: The police put handcuffs on the fleeing suspect.
example.fact: Harry Houdini built much of his early fame on escaping police handcuffs and jail cells in the early 1900s, often asking local officers to search and lock him up in each city he visited as a publicity stunt meant to prove no restraint could hold him.

components.note: 一 (one) — relates to 百's meaning 'hundred,' a large round number built from 'one.'
白 (bái) gives a sound hint — 百 is pronounced bǎi, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
氵 (water) forms the flowing liquid part of the picture.
匚 (a container shape) receives the water — together showing water gathering into one place, the source of 汇's meaning 'to converge, to gather.'

example.hanzi: 这部音乐剧在百老汇上演了整整十年。
example.pinyin: zhè bù yīnyuèjù zài Bǎilǎohuì shàngyǎnle zhěngzhěng shí nián.
example.english: This musical has run on Broadway for a full ten years.
example.fact: Broadway's longest-running show, The Phantom of the Opera, opened in 1988 and played for 35 consecutive years before closing in 2023. Over that run it employed an estimated 6,500 people and grossed more revenue than any other production in theater history.

components.note: 亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.
戈 (a dagger-axe, a weapon) — 战 relates to fighting and war.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 战 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 士兵们在恶劣的天气中继续作战。
example.pinyin: shìbīngmen zài èliè de tiānqì zhōng jìxù zuòzhàn.
example.english: The soldiers continued fighting in the harsh weather.
example.fact: During the WWII Battle of Stalingrad, winter temperatures fell below -30°C. German troops, left with only summer uniforms after Hitler expected a quick victory, suffered tens of thousands of frostbite casualties before the battle ended in February 1943.

meanings: to discuss a paper or thesis

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 论 relates to discussing or explaining something with words.
仑 (logical order, arrangement) — combined with speech, 论 came to mean 'to discuss' or 'a theory,' explaining ideas in an orderly way.
文 depicts a chest marked with crossing lines, once tattoos or patterns on the body — decoration and pattern gave rise to the idea of 'writing' and 'culture.'

example.hanzi: 她正在图书馆里写毕业论文。
example.pinyin: tā zhèngzài túshūguǎn lǐ xiě bìyè lùnwén.
example.english: She is writing her graduation thesis in the library.
example.fact: The modern practice of peer review is often traced to the Royal Society's Philosophical Transactions in the 1660s, though it didn't become standard scientific practice until the 20th century — before then, journal editors alone typically decided what to publish.

components.note: 辶 (to walk, to move) — suggests departing or leaving.
贵 (valuable, precious) — leaving something valuable behind gave 遗 its meaning 'to lose, to leave behind.'
口 (mouth) — 嘱 describes an act of speaking, giving careful instructions.
属 (shǔ) gives a sound close to zhǔ, sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 老人在去世前立下了一份遗嘱。
example.pinyin: lǎorén zài qùshì qián lìxiàle yī fèn yízhǔ.
example.english: The elderly person made a will before passing away.
example.fact: The oldest surviving will in the world is believed to belong to an Egyptian priest named Wah, written around 1800 BC on papyrus and discovered at the site of Thebes. It names his mother as the sole heir to his property.

components.note: 平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
巳 (here representing an eye) — in one traditional theory, this depicted a captive's marked eye, an ancient sign of subjugation, which later broadened to mean 'the common people.'
戈 (a dagger-axe) — combined with the eye shape above, this ties the character to the idea of marking or piercing.

example.hanzi: 战争给平民带来了巨大的痛苦。
example.pinyin: zhànzhēng gěi píngmín dàiláile jùdà de tòngkǔ.
example.english: War brought enormous suffering to civilians.
example.fact: The Fourth Geneva Convention of 1949 was the first international treaty to focus specifically on protecting civilians in wartime, drafted in direct response to the widespread targeting of noncombatant populations during World War II.

components.note: 亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

The oracle-bone form is generally read as a pile of firewood burning, with rising smoke — an image whose original meaning is uncertain. The character was borrowed for its sound to write the grammatical particle marking 'the one who...', the link to fire having faded.

example.hanzi: 这本书的作者是一位年轻的女作家。
example.pinyin: zhè běn shū de zuòzhě shì yī wèi niánqīng de nǚ zuòjiā.
example.english: The author of this book is a young female writer.
example.fact: The identity of Elena Ferrante, author of the internationally acclaimed Neapolitan Novels, remains disputed and unconfirmed to the public. Despite investigative attempts, including a controversial 2016 financial-document analysis, the author has never publicly confirmed a name.

components.note: 夕 (evening/night), doubled — two nights stacked together suggested the idea of accumulation, giving 多 its meaning of 'many, much.'

The simplified form pictures a curling wisp escaping unevenly to one side, evoking breath or vapor leaking out lopsided — an image of something incomplete or short, the source of 亏's meaning 'to lose, deficient, at a disadvantage.'

example.hanzi: 多亏了邻居的帮助,我们才顺利搬完家。
example.pinyin: duōkuī le línjū de bāngzhù, wǒmen cái shùnlì bān wán jiā.
example.english: Thanks to the neighbor's help, we finished moving smoothly.
example.fact: Vampire bats are one of the few mammals known to regularly share regurgitated blood with roost-mates who failed to feed that night. Researchers have found the bats preferentially help individuals who have helped them before — a rare documented case of reciprocal altruism in the wild.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 体 concerns a person's physical form.
本 (root, foundation) — combined with 亻, the character frames the body as a person's basic, foundational form, distinct from the far more complex traditional character 體 it replaced.
千 (thousand) — 重 pictures a heavy burden carried a great distance.
里 (a unit of distance, like a mile) — carrying something a thousand 里 emphasizes how heavy and significant a burden it is, giving 重 its meaning 'heavy' or 'important.'

example.hanzi: 医生建议他控制体重,多运动。
example.pinyin: yīshēng jiànyì tā kòngzhì tǐzhòng, duō yùndòng.
example.english: The doctor advised him to control his body weight and exercise more.
example.fact: Astronauts don't lose actual mass by going into orbit — they float because they and their spacecraft are in continuous free fall around Earth, not because gravity has vanished. At the International Space Station's altitude, Earth's gravity is still about 90% as strong as at the surface.

components.note: The oracle-bone form pictured a house with a window or opening facing a particular way — the direction the opening faced gave 向 its meaning 'direction, toward.'
止, a stylized foot, sits at the top — depicting a step being taken.
舟 (boat), now disguised as 月 and 刀 in the modern form, sits below — a foot stepping onto a boat to advance, the source of 前's meaning 'to advance, front, before.'

example.hanzi: 遇到困难时,我们要勇敢地向前。
example.pinyin: yùdào kùnnán shí, wǒmen yào yǒnggǎn de xiàngqián.
example.english: When facing difficulties, we should bravely move forward.
example.fact: Sea horses are the only fish known to swim upright, propelling themselves forward almost entirely with a dorsal fin that beats up to 30 times per second. That swimming style is so inefficient that sea horses are also among the slowest-moving fish in the ocean.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 伴 describes a person accompanying another.
半 (bàn) is an exact match for the sound of 伴.
亻 (person) — 侣 names a person who accompanies another.
吕 (lǚ) gives the sound — an exact match with 侣.

example.hanzi: 他们是相识多年的老伴侣。
example.pinyin: tāmen shì xiāngshí duōnián de lǎo bànlǚ.
example.english: They are longtime companions who have known each other for years.
example.fact: Albatrosses often mate with the same partner for decades and perform elaborate, synchronized courtship dances that can take years to perfect. Some individuals return to the same mate at the same nesting site every breeding season for over 50 years.

components.note: The oracle-bone form is generally read as a snake with its body curled, or alternatively a person kneeling with an exaggerated limb — the original picture's meaning was largely lost when the character was borrowed purely for its sound, including to write the name of the ancient Ba region in present-day Sichuan.
西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'

example.hanzi: 巴西是世界上咖啡产量最大的国家。
example.pinyin: Bāxī shì shìjiè shàng kāfēi chǎnliàng zuìdà de guójiā.
example.english: Brazil is the world's largest coffee-producing country.
example.fact: Brazil produces roughly a third of the world's coffee supply, a dominance traceable to seedlings smuggled out of French Guiana in 1727. Legend holds that a Portuguese officer received them as a farewell gift from the French governor's wife, planting the seeds that grew into Brazil's coffee industry today.

components.note: 页 (head) — 预 relates to looking ahead or foreseeing beforehand
予 (yǔ) gives a sound close to 预's reading yù, differing mainly in tone
咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'

example.hanzi: 她心里有一种不祥的预感。
example.pinyin: tā xīnlǐ yǒu yī zhǒng bùxiáng de yùgǎn.
example.english: She had an ominous premonition in her heart.
example.fact: Some animals, including catfish and toads, have been observed behaving unusually in the hours before earthquakes, but decades of research have failed to establish a reliable biological early-warning signal. Most scientists attribute reported cases to coincidence or to subtle ground vibrations animals sense just seconds before humans do.

components.note: 囗 (an enclosure) — something firmly closed in is secure, tied to 固's meaning 'solid, firm.'
古 (gǔ) gives a rhyme close to gù, with the tone shifted.
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 书架已经固定在墙上了。
example.pinyin: shūjià yǐjīng gùdìng zài qiáng shàng le.
example.english: The bookshelf has already been fixed to the wall.
example.fact: Ancient astronomers called stars 'fixed' because, unlike the planets (from the Greek for 'wanderers'), they appeared to hold constant positions relative to each other. It wasn't until the 18th century that astronomer Edmund Halley confirmed stars actually do move, just too slowly and too far away for the shift to be visible within a human lifetime.

components.note: 口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.
口 (mouth) — 味 relates to taste, sensed in the mouth.
未 (wèi) gives the sound — an exact match with 味.

example.hanzi: 每个地方的口味都不太一样。
example.pinyin: měi gè dìfang de kǒuwèi dōu bù tài yīyàng.
example.english: The taste preferences are somewhat different in every place.
example.fact: Humans have roughly 10,000 taste buds distributed not just on the tongue but also on the soft palate, throat, and even the epiglottis. Each bud is replaced about every 10 to 14 days, which is part of why a burnt tongue recovers its sense of taste so quickly.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 锻 originally described working metal by heat and force.
段 (duàn) gives the sound — an exact match with 锻.
Fire — refining metal requires heat.
Gives the sound jiǎn, related to liàn but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 坚持锻炼可以让身体更健康。
example.pinyin: jiānchí duànliàn kěyǐ ràng shēntǐ gèng jiànkāng.
example.english: Persisting in exercise can make the body healthier.
example.fact: Regular aerobic exercise has been shown to increase the volume of the hippocampus, a brain region central to memory, even in older adults. A 2011 study found that a year of moderate walking increased hippocampal volume by about 2%, effectively reversing one to two years of age-related shrinkage.

meanings: (coll.) to be interested in (often used in the negative)

components.note: 咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'
目 (eye) — 冒 originally described something extending over or covering, related to a covering over the head.
冃 (mào) is an exact match for the sound of 冒.

example.hanzi: 他昨天淋雨后就感冒了。
example.pinyin: tā zuótiān lín yǔ hòu jiù gǎnmào le.
example.english: He caught a cold after getting caught in the rain yesterday.
example.fact: Over 200 different virus types can cause the common cold, with rhinoviruses responsible for the majority of cases. This enormous viral diversity is the main reason no universal cold vaccine has ever been developed, unlike for many single-pathogen diseases.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
月, appearing twice side by side, originally depicted two people (or two strings of shells) together — giving 朋 its meaning 'friend, companion.'
又 (hand), shown twice and joined together — two hands clasped in friendship gave 友 its meaning 'friend.'

example.hanzi: 公园里有很多小朋友在玩耍。
example.pinyin: gōngyuán lǐ yǒu hěnduō xiǎopéngyǒu zài wánshuǎ.
example.english: There are many children playing in the park.
example.fact: Children's brains reach about 90% of their adult size by age five, but the prefrontal cortex — responsible for judgment and impulse control — continues developing until the mid-20s. That's part of why risk assessment and decision-making mature so much later than overall brain size.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 注 relates to pouring or directing, like water poured into something
主 (zhǔ) gives a sound close to 注's reading zhù
册 is a simplified picture of narrow bamboo strips bound together side by side with a cord, the earliest form of a book in China.

example.hanzi: 新生需要在开学前完成网上注册。
example.pinyin: xīnshēng xūyào zài kāixué qián wánchéng wǎngshàng zhùcè.
example.english: New students need to complete online registration before the semester starts.
example.fact: The first-ever registered .com domain name, symbolics.com, was registered on March 15, 1985, by a now-defunct computer company. It predates the World Wide Web itself by six years and is preserved today as a piece of internet history rather than used commercially.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 遭 relates to something you come across or run into on your way.
曹 (cáo) gives a sound distantly related to zāo, having drifted apart over time.
爫 (a hand, from above) — 受 pictures something being passed.
又 (a hand, from below) — one hand giving and another receiving gave 受 its meaning 'to receive' or 'to endure.'

example.hanzi: 这座城市遭受了严重的洪灾。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò chéngshì zāoshòule yánzhòng de hóngzāi.
example.english: This city suffered severe flood damage.
example.fact: The 1931 China floods along the Yangtze and Huai rivers are considered by many historians to be the deadliest natural disaster ever recorded, with death toll estimates ranging from several hundred thousand to over 4 million once the resulting famine and disease are factored in.

components.note: Flesh — swelling happens on the body.
Gives the sound zhōng, related to zhǒng but drifted apart over time.
疒 (sickness) — 瘤 names a medical growth.
留 (liú) gives the sound — an exact match with 瘤.

example.hanzi: 医生通过检查发现了一个良性肿瘤。
example.pinyin: yīshēng tōngguò jiǎnchá fāxiànle yī gè liángxìng zhǒngliú.
example.english: The doctor discovered a benign tumor through an examination.
example.fact: Tumors aren't unique to humans — paleontologists have identified likely cancerous growths in fossilized dinosaur bones dating back over 70 million years, including a probable case of osteosarcoma found in a Centrosaurus fibula described in a 2020 study.

components.note: 气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.
口 (mouth) — 味 relates to taste, sensed in the mouth.
未 (wèi) gives the sound — an exact match with 味.

example.hanzi: 厨房里飘出一阵诱人的气味。
example.pinyin: chúfáng lǐ piāo chū yī zhèn yòurén de qìwèi.
example.english: An enticing smell drifted out from the kitchen.
example.fact: A 2014 study published in Science found that the human nose can distinguish over one trillion different odors — far more than the roughly 10,000 estimate long assumed in earlier textbooks, revealing that human olfaction is far more powerful than commonly believed.
